key_insight: Scaling Representation Autoencoders (RAEs) by training large diffusion-transformer decoders on a frozen high‑dimensional semantic encoder (SigLIP‑2) enables open‑domain text‑to‑image generation; scale improves general image fidelity but achieving strong text alignment requires targeted data composition.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between RAE-based diffusion models (previously successful on ImageNet) and large‑scale, freeform text‑to‑image generation—addressing how to scale architectures and data to preserve visual fidelity while maintaining text conditioning.
method: Freeze a high‑capacity semantic encoder (SigLIP‑2) to produce stable, high‑dimensional representation latents.
Scale diffusion‑transformer decoders (RAE decoders) trained in the encoder's semantic latent space for image reconstruction and generation.
Train on a mixed corpus (web images, synthetic renders, and text‑rendered data) and analyze how dataset composition impacts fidelity and text alignment.
impact: Provides a modular, scalable recipe for building high‑fidelity T2I models by decoupling representation encoding from generative decoding—enabling reuse of frozen encoders and focused decoder scaling, while highlighting the importance of targeted data curation for text alignment.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: frozen SigLIP‑2 encoder -> semantic latent space -> large diffusion transformer decoder (RAE).
Data composition pie chart: web images vs synthetic vs text‑rendered, annotated with their impact on fidelity vs text alignment.
Performance tradeoff chart: decoder scale (model size) vs image fidelity and text alignment (qualitative metric curves).
Qualitative grid: sample prompts with generated images illustrating improvements from scaling and from curated data.
paper_title: Scaling Text-to-Image Diffusion Transformers with Representation Autoencoders
paper_authors: Shengbang Tong, Boyang Zheng, Ziteng Wang, Bingda Tang, Nanye Ma
